Flagrant

FLAY-grunt -- Latin flagrare, 'to burn, blaze': a flagrant offense burns in plain sight. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Flagrant is obviously offensive or shameless.

Copying an entire essay word for word is a flagrant case of cheating.

Worked Example

A driver rolls slowly past a stopped school bus with its red lights flashing and its stop arm out, waves at the bus driver, and keeps going.

Wrongdoing done openly, with no attempt to hide it, is exactly what flagrant describes. Unlike 'serious,' which is only about size, flagrant is about how obvious and shameless the offense is.

How Flagrant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

obvious

obvious: easy for anyone to see

outrageous

outrageous: shocking enough to cause anger

blatant

blatant: done openly with no attempt to hide it

Antonyms

concealed

concealed: kept out of sight

trivial

trivial: too small to matter

How Strong Is It? — obvious → flagrant → outrageous

obvious vs. flagrant

obvious vs. flagrant: Obvious is neutral where flagrant is damning -- an obvious answer is simply easy to see, while a flagrant act is easy to see and plainly wrong.

outrageous vs. flagrant

outrageous vs. flagrant: Outrageous is flagrant plus fury: a flagrant violation is openly and shamelessly wrong, while an outrageous one is wrong enough to make people genuinely angry.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — flagr-

root — flagr-: to burn, to blaze (Latin (flagrare))

suffix — -ant

suffix — -ant: adjective-forming: doing the action (Latin (-antem))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin flagrans meant 'blazing, burning,' from flagrare ('to burn') -- a flagrant offense blazes away in full view of everyone, from the same root behind conflagration, a great fire.

Use the root in a new word: conflagration

Use the root in a new word: conflagration: A single spilled lantern grew into a conflagration that swept through six blocks.

Root Check

Word Choice

Flagrant attaches to wrongdoing: a flagrant foul, a flagrant lie, a flagrant violation. It always disapproves, and it stresses that the offender did not even bother to hide what they were doing.
